package_info.package_versions: All UI builds deployed to IPFS since January 1, 2024
package_info.why_malicious: A developer inserted malicious JavaScript into the Tornado Cash user interface, which covertly exfiltrated users’ private deposit notes to an attacker-controlled server, enabling theft of funds. This was a supply chain attack hidden in a governance proposal, targeting users accessing the UI via IPFS gateways.

execution_context.trigger: At runtime, when a user interacts with deposit or withdrawal functions in the Tornado Cash UI
execution_context.file_location: JavaScript source code of the Tornado Cash web UI (deployed on IPFS gateways), specifically in modules handling deposit note management
required_permissions: Access to in-memory deposit notes or private keys

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when a user interacts with deposit or withdrawal functions, the code accesses the user's private deposit note in memory, encodes it, and sends it via HTTPS POST to a hardcoded attacker-controlled domain, resulting in covert exfiltration of sensitive credentials.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code accesses sensitive cryptographic material (the user's private deposit note) and transmits it to an external, attacker-controlled server without any legitimate reason or user notification.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: The legitimate Tornado Cash UI should never transmit private deposit notes or cryptographic keys off-device; all cryptographic operations and sensitive data handling are expected to remain strictly local to the user's browser.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate analytics or telemetry code may send anonymized, non-sensitive usage data to trusted domains, but never private keys, deposit notes, or any cryptographic secrets.
key_indicators: Direct access to in-memory cryptographic secrets (deposit notes)
Network request to a hardcoded, non-Tornado Cash external domain
Encoding and transmission of user secrets without user consent
Absence of user notification or opt-in for data transmission
Code introduced via governance proposal or non-standard code path

attack_chain.action: Malicious JavaScript is inserted into the Tornado Cash UI codebase via a deceptive developer contribution hidden in a governance proposal.
attack_chain.leads_to: Deployment of compromised UI to IPFS gateways

attack_chain.action: Users access the compromised Tornado Cash UI via public IPFS gateways (e.g., ipfs.io, cf-ipfs.com), unknowingly loading the malicious code in their browsers.
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of malicious code in users' browsers

attack_chain.action: When users interact with deposit or withdrawal functions, the malicious code captures their private deposit notes in memory.
attack_chain.leads_to: Exfiltration of deposit notes to attacker

attack_chain.action: Attacker receives the exfiltrated deposit notes and uses them to access and steal users' funds from Tornado Cash.

behavioral_signatures: JavaScript code in the Tornado Cash UI accessing deposit notes or private keys in memory during user interaction
Network requests from the UI to hardcoded, non-Tornado Cash external domains, especially during deposit or withdrawal operations
Encoding and exfiltration of sensitive user data (deposit notes) as part of normal UI workflows
file_indicators: Unexpected JavaScript code in Tornado Cash UI source referencing external domains not associated with the official project
Obfuscated or hidden code blocks introduced via governance proposal merges or non-standard code review paths
Presence of fetch or XMLHttpRequest calls targeting unknown endpoints within modules handling deposit notes
network_indicators: HTTPS POST requests from user browsers to attacker-controlled domains (e.g., https://attacker-server.com/collect) originating from the Tornado Cash UI
Outbound connections from IPFS-hosted Tornado Cash UI to domains not listed in the official project documentation
Unusual data payloads containing encoded deposit notes or cryptographic material sent to external servers
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Continuously monitor the Tornado Cash UI JavaScript for any code that accesses deposit notes or private keys and transmits them to external domains. Use browser or network monitoring tools to detect POST requests to non-official endpoints, especially during deposit or withdrawal actions. Audit all code contributions, with special scrutiny for those merged via governance proposals, for hidden or obfuscated network exfiltration logic. Flag any JavaScript code that references external domains not present in the official repository or documentation.
